title: Per route schemas for params, query and body
when: An API checks inputs ad hoc inside each handler and the user wants one validation layer where every route declares the shape of its path params, query string and JSON body.
prompt:
Goal: Each route declares a schema; one step coerces and checks params, query and body, and the handler only sees clean values.
Steps:
1. Declare schemas as plain objects: { params: { id: uuid() }, query: { limit: int({ min: 1, max: 100, def: 20 }) }, body: { title: str({ max: 200 }), done: bool({ optional: true }) } }.
2. Write field builders in validate.mjs (str, int, bool, enumOf, uuid, isoDate) that return { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, reason }.
3. Query values arrive as text: turn "20" into 20 and "true" into true only through a builder; accept repeated keys (?tag=a&tag=b) only where the schema says list.
4. Unknown body keys give 422 by default, so a typo like "titel" is not silently dropped.
5. Collect all failures into { error: "invalid_input", fields: { "body.title": "too long" } } and answer 422 once.
6. Attach the schema when registering: router.add("POST", "/tasks", { schema }, handler); the handler reads ctx.input.
Quality bar:
- No handler reads req.url or the raw body itself.
- Every string and number has a limit.
- Schemas also feed the API docs.
Pitfalls:
- Number("") is 0 and Number("1e3") is 1000; match integers with /^-?\d+$/ first.
- Validating after the write.
- Different error shapes for params and body.
Verify:
- [ ] Every route has a schema, even an empty one.
- [ ] Unknown body keys give 422.
- [ ] Tests feed "", "abc" and "007" to int.
- [ ] One response lists every field error.
Output: validate.mjs, a schema beside each route, test/validate.test.mjs.

examples.input: quero validar params, query e body de todas as rotas num lugar so
examples.output: int/str/bool builders, schema per route, 422 with a fields map, unknown keys refused
